newsitem.title: UK: Airtours says expects to be cleared by MMC.
newsitem.headline: Airtours says expects to be cleared by MMC.

text.p: UK tour operator Airotours said on Thursday that it expected to be cleared by a Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) probe into the travel industry.
"We are disappointed but we don't think there is a case to answer," said Airtours deputy chief executive Harry Coe.
"We will just face some irritating distractions over the next 12 months and then they'll say "carry on as you were boys'," he told Reuters in an interview.

The OFT on Thursday asked the MMC to investigate links between leading tour operators and travel agency chains. The MMC will also look at the practice among travel agents of offering holidays at a discount conditional on the purchase of specific travel insurance.
It said that the referral followed fruitless talks with Airtours and market leader Thomson, part of Canada's Thomson Corp.
Thomson owns the market leading Lunn Poly travel agency while number two tour operator Airtours owns the second largest travel agency Going Places.
Coe said that Airtours had been prepared to give the undertakings sought by the OFT to avoid a referral. The implication is that Thomson had been unwilling to do so.
He said that Britain offered the world's cheapest foreign holiday packages.
"If you take a walk down the high street you see that there is an incredible selection and choice at much lower prices than people were paying 10-15 years ago."
"Those behind the inquiry are the small tour operators and the small travel agents who can't stand the heat in the kitchen," he added.
Coe said that about 10 million packages were sold to Britons each year at an average price of around 350 stg a head.
He said that discounts had to be tied to the sale of travel insurance because margins on the actual holidays were so slim -- as low as one percent for a 350 stg package.
But he said that Airtours would have no problems if the MMC ordered the sale of insurance to be disconnected from discounts.
